setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-note pattern. The song has one slot, Song 01, at the full global length of 64 steps, with Song mode AUTO, and the sequencer is stopped. The norns is showing the Pattern editor, left over from setup; it is not part of this lesson.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Song (6,8). The Playback screen lists Playing SONG 01, Next SONG 01, Pass 1/1, Global length 64 and Song mode AUTO. The global length fader is on grid row 7: (1,7) subtracts one step, (8,7) adds one, and the buttons between jump to 1, 13, 32, 38, 51 and 64.
steps.title: Open the Song editor

steps.caption: Tap the fader's left end (1,7). It takes one step off the length and the Playback screen shows Global length 63. To loop a short fragment instead, jump with (2,7) to 1 step and add steps with (8,7); see the recipe on this page.
steps.title: Shorten by one step

steps.caption: Tap the fader's right end (8,7), which adds one step. Global length reads 64 again, so the whole phrase plays.
steps.title: Return to 64 steps

steps.caption: Tap (2,7), which jumps to 1 step, then tap (8,7) once to add one. Global length reads 2. Press Play (1,8): the song plays only its first two steps and starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is C and D (60, 62) over and over, never E or F. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Set the length to 2 steps and play

steps.caption: Tap (8,7) twice. Global length reads 4. Press Play: the whole four-note phrase now plays before the song starts again, so the MIDI sent in this step is 60, 62, 64, 65. Press Play again to stop.
steps.title: Set the length to 4 steps and play

steps.caption: Tap (7,7), the button that jumps to 64. Global length reads 64 again and the whole phrase is available to the song.
steps.title: Return to 64
